\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{v_i \in W} \sum_{v_j \in W} \lVert v_i - v_j \rVert
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(W\): The color vectors of the window
- \(v_i, v_j\): Color vectors in the window
- \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\): The L1 or L2 distance

W holds the color vectors (R, G, B) of the window. For each one, the filter adds up its distances to all the others. The vector with the smallest sum is the output. On a tie, the first vector in reading order wins. For a gray image, this is the plain median.
